author: Copilot
body: Sentry init currently runs whenever `STACK_ENVIRONMENT` is set, even if the DSN is explicitly overridden to an empty string. The docs/README describe `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN=""` as a supported way to disable Sentry, but this code will still call `get_sentry_config()` and `sentry_sdk.init()` with an empty DSN (which may raise during DSN parsing or at least defeats the intent of an explicit disable). Consider gating initialization on a non-empty DSN (and/or normalizing blank DSNs to None in `SentrySettings`).

author: Copilot
Copilot
body: Sentry is initialized whenever `STACK_ENVIRONMENT` is set, even if `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN` is overridden to an empty string. `sentry_sdk.init(dsn="")` may raise and prevent the service from starting. Gate initialization on a non-empty DSN (and/or normalize empty DSN to `None` in settings) so `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN=""` reliably disables Sentry as documented.

author: Copilot
body: This documentation says `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN=""` explicitly disables Sentry, but the current MCP settings/lifespan code will still attempt `sentry_sdk.init` with the configured DSN. Either update the code to treat empty DSN as disabled, or adjust the docs to match actual behavior to avoid broken deployments.

author: Copilot
body:
The config table claims `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN=""` disables Sentry. Ensure the runtime behavior matches this (i.e., empty DSN is normalized to disabled and Sentry init is skipped), or update the README to avoid instructing a configuration that can break startup.
```suggestion
| `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN` | built-in default DSN | Sentry reporting is enabled when `STACK_ENVIRONMENT` is set. Override with a custom DSN as needed. |
```

author: Copilot
body: Previously the MCP HTTP sub-app was created with `stateless_http=True`; now `mcp.http_app(path="/")` relies on the FastMCP default. Given the README states requests are stateless and session headers are ignored, it would be safer to pass `stateless_http=True` explicitly (or otherwise ensure the default remains stateless) to avoid accidentally enabling server-side session state across upgrades.

author: Copilot
body: The docs/README say Sentry can be explicitly disabled by setting `PORTAL_SENTRY_DSN=""`, but this lifespan hook still initializes Sentry whenever `STACK_ENVIRONMENT` is set, even if the DSN is an empty string. That can lead to an attempted init with an invalid DSN and does not match the documented disable behavior. Consider skipping `sentry_sdk.init()` when `sentry_settings.dsn` is blank (or normalizing blank -> None in settings) and gating on both `stack_environment` and a non-empty DSN.

author: Copilot
body:
This module duplicates the handler-import side-effect pattern that already exists in `portal.mcp.routes.tools.attach_mcp_routes()`. Keeping two separate entry points that must stay in sync increases the chance of drift (e.g., a new handler added to one list but not the other). Consider consolidating on a single canonical registration module and having other callers import from it.
```suggestion
from portal.mcp.routes.tools import attach_mcp_routes
from portal.mcp.tools.server import mcp

# Reuse the canonical MCP route/tool registration entry point so handler
# imports stay centralized in one place.
attach_mcp_routes()
```
